subject: Sibling
hook: SIBLING IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Full siblings do not actually share exactly 50% of their DNA; due to the nature of chromosomal crossover, the actual amount of shared DNA varies significantly, with a quarter of sibling pairs sharing either more than 52.76% or less than 47.8% of their genetic material.
angle_support: In practice, full siblings do not share exactly 50% of their DNA, as chromosomal crossover only occurs a limited number of times and, therefore, large chunks of a chromosome are shared or not shared at one time.
In fact, the mean DNA fraction shared is 50.28% with a standard deviation of 3.68%, meaning approximately 1/4 of sibling pairs share more than 52.76% of their DNA, while 1/4 share less than 47.8%.
title: Why You Don't Actually Share 50% DNA With Siblings
description: While people assume siblings share exactly half of their genetic material, biological reality is much more variable due to how chromosomes are passed down. This video explains why the 50% rule is just an average, not a guarantee.
narration: SIBLING IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture full siblings as sharing exactly fifty percent of their DNA. It feels like a mathematical certainty because they share the same two parents. But this assumption is wrong. The reality is far more random, and the actual genetic overlap varies quite significantly between siblings. Chromosomal crossover happens only a limited number of times during the creation of egg and sperm cells. Because these large chunks of genetic material are inherited in bundles rather than perfectly split, the average shared DNA is about fifty point twenty-eight percent. In fact, a full quarter of sibling pairs share either more than fifty-two percent or less than forty-seven percent of their unique genetic code. Your brother or sister is less of a genetic mirror than you have always been led to believe.
